question: Can the p65 Supervisor persist its slot registry when the staged loader starts it through NSH exec?
prototype_hypothesis: The registry file cannot be written from the supervisor's call path on this firmware, so the installer has to publish it.
callsite_evidence: Raw open 0x1c1580e4 opens existing files for writing from the exec context (six flag encodings all succeed) but creating a new file returns ENOENT with every encoding tried (1, 2, 0x41, 0x241, 0x401, 0x201 and the MIwear 2/0x4 pair) in /tmp, /data, /data/misc, /data/app and /data/canopus.
A write() to a file descriptor opened in the exec context resets the emulated device (console descriptor writes work; PRIMASK and BASEPRI are 0 and a 16 KiB stack changes nothing).
Lua io.open(path, "wb") creates files in the same device from the watchface task, so the VFS itself can create - the supervisor's call path is what fails.

With canopus_supervisor_save_registry persisting through /canopus/registry instead, the installer's five steps all return COMPLETED, /data/canopus/registry.bin holds 784 bytes (magic CRD1, version 2) and the Manager page reports the registry as ready with 0 filesystem errors.
control_flow_evidence: The serialized registry is produced by canopus_supervisor_serialize_registry and served read-only through a third pseudo-inode (/canopus/registry); the installer face writes it with io.open and verifies the readback.
ownership_analysis: No new ownership; the registry device lives in the supervisor's own inode namespace next to /canopus/install.
unsafe_assumptions: Emulator evidence only (host/emulator level); no physical device has run this.
Deferred persistence means a slot change made while no installer page runs stays in RAM until the installer publishes it.
Only the five installer steps were exercised; module install/update/remove paths were not re-run.
recommended_probe: Install a real .canopus module through the installer and confirm the slot survives a reboot.
